extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology claims from XML/PDF sections, figure captions, and local OA figure assets.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: RRP9W4N, GRR10W4N, and related W/F end-tagged PRELP-derived peptides
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Direct bacterial and model-membrane permeabilization assays support membrane-directed activity, with source evidence showing stronger action on bacteria/anionic liposomes than on zwitterionic cholesterol-containing liposomes.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Recorded as membrane permeabilization/selectivity evidence; it does not prove a single pore architecture or exclude non-membrane contributions.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: RRP9WWWW-NH2 and selected W/F end-tagged peptides
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Protease-stability and blood/skin infection assays provide source-supported functional selectivity context for the optimized W-tagged peptide, while toxicity remains bounded by hemolysis/cell assays rather than inferred as absent for every derivative.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Functional efficacy and selectivity context is separated from direct molecular mechanism; exact graph-only values are not normalized outside the source.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C-terminal W/F end-tagged GRR10/RRP9 sequence series
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Table 1 and Figure 1 support a structure-activity trend in which C-terminal hydrophobic tagging changes antimicrobial potency and hemolysis; longer tags are cautionary for toxicity.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Trend claim only; exact hemolysis percentages for database rows remain preserved as graph-derived cautions.
